Etymology: 13. BMAC *ǰaǰʰa/ukă̄, OIA jáhakā-, YAv. dužuka-, Bal. ǰǎjuk, dužux, Pers. žūža all ‘hedgehog’; cognate prob. also B. śajāru ‘porcupine’ — Common Kartvelian *ʒaʒ- ‘rat’, Common Sindy *ʒăʒ-ă ‘weasel; pine marten’, Bezhit ǯa͜ǯu ‘hedgehog’. Note: I have suggested in an article (2017a: 16f.) for the South Asian ‘hedgehog’ forms borrowing from Austro-Asiatic. Meanwhile, I find the Kartvelian alterna- tive slightly better and simpler even though semantically it is less straightfor- ward.
